title: Cross-tenant Degradation Correlation and SLA Exploration
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Overview

This document defines the cross-tenant degradation correlation and SLA exploration pattern we use at Redwood Inference to detect, visualize, and triage multi-tenant performance regressions that affect SLA, cost, or model-quality signals. It is intended for platform operators, oncall engineers, and observability engineers who own dashboards/alerts for the runtime and gateway layers.

Purpose

- Provide a reproducible set of dashboard panels, query examples, and runbook steps for rapid cross-tenant impact analysis.
- Standardize correlation heatmaps across service tiers (hosted, dedicated, private) so product teams understand degradation scope.
- Balance signal fidelity and telemetry cost by recommending retention/aggregation rules.

Scope

Applies to the following services and telemetry sources:
- runtime-api (text generation, chat endpoints)
- routing-proxy (smart-routing, fallback)
- kv-prefix-cache (prefix/KV caching layer)
- job-queue (batching & background inference workers)
- cost-metrics (token_count, embedding_units)
- tracers (distributed traces for request-scoped latency)

Audience

- Platform operators (primary)
- SRE oncall and incident commander
- Observability engineers implementing dashboards and alerts
- Product owners for Dedicated and Private offerings

Key Signals and Definitions

- Tenant: logical customer identifier (tenant_id header).
- Service-level SLOs of interest:
  - runtime-api.p95_latency <= 200ms (foreground conversational routes)
  - runtime-api.error_rate <= 0.5% (5m rolling)
  - kv-prefix-cache.hit_rate >= 80% (tenant-level)
  - platform.token_cost_rate <= budgeted_cpu_equivalent (per-tenant monthly commit)
- Cross-tenant degradation: when 5%+ of active tenants exceed their SLA for more than 10 minutes and the aggregate SLO burn rate increases by > 2x baseline.

Dashboard Patterns (panel-level spec)

Use the sections below as implementation templates for Grafana (Prometheus datasource) or Metabase. Keep tenant cardinality controls (top-N, heatmap) and sampling for high-cardinality tenants.

1) Cross-tenant SLO heatmap (Primary pane)
- Description: 1-minute rollup heatmap showing tenant_id vs SLO dimension (p50/p95/p99, error_rate). Color = normalized burn (0=healthy 1=failing).
- Query sketch (PromQL):
  - heatmap_series = heatmap(over_time( (rate(runtime_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"runtime-api\"}[5m])) by (tenant_id, le), 1m))
  - derived_burn = ((p95_latency - p95_target) / p95_target) clipped to [0,4]
- Visualization tips: enable interactive tenant drilldown and a slider to switch window to 5/15/60m.

2) Tenant impact distribution (Top-N list)
- Description: sortable table of tenants contributing to SLO burn with columns: tenant_id, active_requests_per_min, p95_latency, error_rate_5m, kv_hit_rate, token_rate, inferred_cause (see correlation score below).
- Backend queries: composite join from metrics and cost-metrics; use cached materialized view updated every minute for performance.

3) Correlation matrix and causal hints (Adjacency graph)
- Description: matrix correlating tenant-level anomalies across services (rows) vs symptoms (columns: high-p95, increased-queue-depth, trace-errors, low-kv-hit). Cells show Pearson correlation (30m window) and a simple heuristic score (0-100) used for prioritization.
- Implementation note: precompute correlation using a streaming job (kafka -> flink/beam) every 5m to avoid expensive on-the-fly queries.

4) Request path trace rollup pane
- Description: aggregated flamegraphs for failed/slow requests grouped by tenant and model-variant. Include median KV latency and fraction of requests that hit cached prefixes.
- Trace sample policy: 1/100 slow requests, plus deterministic sampling for any request that crosses p99 in a 5m window.

Alerting and Thresholds

We recommend the following alerts and routing patterns. Alerts should reference the dashboard panels and include links to runbook sections.

- Alert: Cross-tenant SLO Burn (P1)
  - Condition: global SLO burn rate > 2x baseline for 10 minutes AND > 5% of active tenants report individual burn > 1.0.
  - Pager: SRE oncall, platform-owners channel (#platform-p1).
  - Runbook link: steps 1–6 in the Runbook section below.

- Alert: Tenant Token Surge (P2)
  - Condition: tenant token_rate > commit * 1.5 for 15 minutes OR token_rate burst > 1M tokens/min sustained 2m.
  - Pager: tenant-ops (owner) + platform oncall.

- Alert: Runtime Cache Collapse (P1)
  - Condition: global kv-prefix-cache.hit_rate < 60% and per-tenant eviction_rate > 0.5% over 5m.
  - Pager: cache-team, platform oncall.

Correlation Score (heuristic)

To help triage, dashboards present an "inferred_cause" derived field computed as a weighted score of correlated signals:
- weights: p95_latency: 0.4, error_rate: 0.25, queue_depth: 0.15, kv_evictions: 0.1, token_burst: 0.1
- score normalization: map to 0-100.
- inference labels: network, kernel-interference, model-variant-saturation, cache-thrashing, tenant-behavioral-burst.

Runbook: Immediate triage steps (for SRE oncall)

1) Confirm the signal
  - Open Cross-tenant SLO heatmap. Toggle time window to 10m then 30m. Identify top 10 tenants by burn.
  - Check related alert logs and correlate with deploy windows (deploy-service timeline).

2) Narrow scope
  - Run: tenant_top = topk(10, sum by (tenant_id)(rate(runtime_api_requests_total[5m])))
  - If top 3 tenants account for >50% of burn, tag incident as "tenant-concentrated" and page tenant success.

3) Surface contributing services
  - Use correlation matrix to check which services have high adjacency score for those tenants.
  - If runtime-api and kv-prefix-cache both score > 60, prioritize cache investigation (see cache runbook).

4) Apply mitigations
  - Temporary mitigations: enable tenant-specific rate-limiter (soft 30% reduction), enable model-variant fallback to smaller quantized variant, or open temporary burst-credit for committed tenants.
  - If mitigation alters burn, note in incident timeline and escalate to deployment rollback if necessary.

5) Deep diagnostics
  - Pull traces for impacted tenants: filter by tenant_id and duration > p95. Attach 5 traces to incident ticket.
  - Run kernel-level profiling on candidate hosts (gpu-fleet profiling job) if kernel-interference tag is inferred.

6) Post-incident actions
  - Create postmortem if incident P1 or if > 2 hours to remediation. Link taxonomy tags: "cross-tenant", "cache", "tenant-burst".
  - Recommended follow-ups: increase KV cache partitions for affected shards; create tenant-specific traffic shaping rule; run tenant-usage review with Customer Success.

Visualization and UX Patterns

- Heatmap sizing: use logarithmic color ramps for token_rate to emphasize high-impact tenants without overwhelming small tenants.
- Drilldown affordances: every tenant row must link to a tenant detail page with last 7 days metrics and cost attribution.
- Export: enable CSV export for top-N lists and automatic attachment to incident tickets.

Telemetry cost & retention guidelines

| Signal | Recommended retention | Aggregation level | Notes |
|--------|-----------------------|-------------------|-------|
| per-request traces | 7 days full, 30 days sampled | request-level | Sample policy described above |
| tenant-level time-series (latency, errors) | 90 days at 1m, 365 days at 5m | tenant x metric | Use TTL and rollup to reduce cardinality |
| prefix-cache events | 30 days | shard-level + per-tenant aggregated | Keep full eviction logs for 30d for debug |
| cost metrics | 365 days | tenant-monthly / daily | Required for billing reconciliations |

Implementation roadmap and milestones (Q4 2025 -> Q2 2026)

- Q4 2025: Prototype heatmap + top-N panel; implement streaming correlation job (Flink). Owner: Observability team.
- Jan 2026: Integrate tenant drilldown and trace rollup; add initial alerts (Cross-tenant SLO Burn, Tenant Token Surge). Owner: Platform SRE.
- Feb 2026: Scale materialized views and add correlation precomputation; run two game days focused on multi-tenant cache collapse. Owner: Platform & Eng-Platform.
- Mar 2026: Harden mitigations (tenant rate limits, auto-fallback to quantized model variants). Owner: Runtime and Platform teams.

Ownership, SLAs, and Escalation

- Dashboard owner: Observability team (primary), Platform SRE (secondary).
- Alert routing: P1 -> SRE oncall + platform owners; P2 -> platform owners + tenant success.
- SLA to maintain dashboard availability: 99.9% during business hours. If dashboard backend is degraded, fallback views must be available with 5m-lag metrics.

Operational Playbooks (short-cuts)

- Rapid rollback: how to rollback a model variant deployment for a single tenant: steps, CLI commands, and safety checks.
- Tenant soft-quarantine: apply a 10m soft-rate limit via OPA policy; sample CLI snippet included.
- Chargeback snapshot: export token and cost rates for top 20 tenants and create report for finance.

Appendix: Example queries and snippets

PromQL (top 10 tenants by p95):
  - topk(10, quantile_over_time(0.95, rate(runtime_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"runtime-api\"}[5m]) by (tenant_id)))

Caching eviction alert (example threshold):
  - sum by (shard)(increase(kv_evictions_total[5m])) / sum by (shard)(increase(kv_lookups_total[5m])) > 0.005

OPA policy snippet (soft rate limit):
  - package platform.rate_limit
  - default allow = true
  - allow { input.request.tenant in deny_list }

Related reading and links

- Platform degradation explainability standards (internal)
- Multi-tenant incident simulation framework (runbook)
